chapter: Chicago memories and the road to the Navy
title: Musicians' dress then and now
summary: Dance and Marge note musicians in the old days were sharp dressers in tie and white shirt, whereas today they look like they came off the farm.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well of course I can understand ....
And in those days, you see, now the prostitutes don't hang around the musicians. They're on the street making money.
Well also I mean in those days the musicians were, were, were more glamorous.

They dressed well and they looked you know, whereas today, now you see musicians come out in their, you know, they look as though they've just come off the farm or something. Leather jackets and jeans and things like that.
In those days musicians, you knew a musician the way he dressed.

As I said, around the union you never saw a musician in there that didn't have on a neck tie and white shirt and dressed nice. Now you go down the union, on occasion I have to go down there too, the bums that drag in the line and all to pay their dues.
Well that's one thing Marge, but the other thing is when you see them on the stand
dressed like bums. I mean, that's what....
You see, that doesn't make sense.
